title: Irrigation Water Chemistry: pH, Alkalinity, EC and Source Risk
summary: Water quality cannot be summarized by a single pH or EC reading; alkalinity, ion composition, source history and contaminant risk answer different questions about irrigation suitability.

sections.title: pH and alkalinity are different measurements
sections.body: pH describes current hydrogen-ion activity while alkalinity describes acid-neutralizing capacity, commonly driven by bicarbonates and carbonates. Repeated high-alkalinity irrigation can influence substrate pH even when a one-time pH reading appears only moderately basic.

sections.title: EC measures bulk conductivity, not ion identity
sections.body: Electrical conductivity responds to dissolved ions collectively and is valuable for salinity and concentration trends, but two waters with similar EC can contain very different proportions of sodium, calcium, chloride, bicarbonate or nutrients. Element-specific questions require element-specific analysis.

sections.title: Source risk extends beyond routine chemistry
sections.body: A 2026 cannabis reclaimed-water study found that acceptable general physicochemical performance did not eliminate every product-contaminant concern, demonstrating why source-specific chemical and microbiological monitoring may be needed in addition to routine pH and EC.
